2607.17713.title: AEGIS: Awareness-Enhanced Guidance for Iterative Safeguard
2607.17713.paper_summary: Span-level rationales are often assumed to improve controllability in text detoxification, but it remains unclear when such guidance helps and when it introduces trade-offs. We present Awareness-Enhanced Guidance for Iterative Safeguard (AEGIS) as an exploratory framework for studying span-guided multilingual detoxification across English, Mandarin Chinese, and Korean. AEGIS combines span-level detector outputs with frozen generator backbones, allowing harmful spans, intensity labels, and target attributes to be provided as structured guidance during rewriting. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art detoxification performance, we analyze how span guidance affects the balance between toxicity reduction and meaning preservation across generator families, model scales, and languages. Our results suggest that span-guided detoxification is conditionally useful: explicit rationales change the trade-off between toxicity reduction and meaning preservation, but their effects depend strongly on the generator backbone and the linguistic context. These findings highlight both the promise and the limitations of span-level control signals for multilingual detoxification.
2607.17713.paper_summary_zh: <span-level>的理據通常被認為能改善文本去毒化的可控性，但何時這種指導有助於改善，何時又會引入權衡仍不清楚。<lb/>我們提出了增強意識的迭代保障指導（AEGIS），作為一個探索性框架，用於研究跨英語、普通話和韓語的<span-guided>多語言去毒化。<lb/>AEGIS將<span-level>檢測器輸出與固定的生成器骨幹結合，允許在重寫過程中提供有害<span>、強度標籤和目標屬性作為結構化指導。<lb/>我們並不聲稱擁有最先進的去毒化性能，而是分析<span>指導如何影響在生成器家族、模型規模和語言之間的毒性減少與意義保留之間的平衡。<lb/>我們的結果表明，基於<span>的去毒化在條件上是有用的：明確的理據改變了毒性減少與意義保留之間的權衡，但它們的影響在很大程度上取決於生成器骨幹和語言上下文。<lb/>這些發現突顯了<span-level>控制信號在多語言去毒化中的潛力和局限性。</span-level>
